samples.identity: Raw multipart PHP session-upload-progress inclusion exploit probe
behavior: Sets PHPSESSID and targets its /var/lib/php/session/sess_ file via page=
Places PHP tags in multipart filename while enabling PHP_SESSION_UPLOAD_PROGRESS
Calls system(base64_decode(aWQ=)), decoding to id, between response markers
samples.judgment: MALICIOUS exploit payload: explicit session-file poisoning plus inclusion crosses a PHP code-execution boundary. target.invalid and response markers are consistent with a proof of concept; they do not establish an authorized deployment.
samples.limits: A raw request is not a sender program. Success depends on vulnerable page inclusion, session storage/progress settings, and timing. No request was transmitted.
samples.coverage: Three hostile exploit findings and three suspicious findings remain unchanged.
samples.marker_line: PHP session probe: poisons upload filename and includes session for RCE

samples.identity: Minimal C socket-command dispatch source fragment
behavior: recv writes network input into command
popen(command, r) passes that same input to a command shell
samples.judgment: MALICIOUS on balance: the fragment exposes arbitrary received command text directly to a shell without any local command restriction. A legitimate remote administrator could use this primitive, but the sample supplies no authentication, administrative protocol, or stated legitimate function.
samples.limits: No main, connect/listen, output relay, persistence, or caller is present. It does not demonstrate a reverse shell, successful execution, or absence of authentication elsewhere. It ignores recv result and does not terminate the buffer; execution can fail or read beyond the received data.
samples.provenance: Byte-identical to the existing socket-commands.c positive regression control in testdata/triage/acquit-second-review; that correspondence supplies no deployment authorization or original acquisition provenance.
samples.coverage: Two accurate suspicious dispatch traits retained. No hostile trait is added: caller and access context are absent.
samples.marker_line: Socket shell handler: recv feeds popen; dispatch trait relocated

Crypto imports use AST import specifiers and module names, rejecting comments and unrelated modules.

classifier_comparison: PHP remains hostile (0.999868); C remains hostile (0.998031 to 0.998957); JavaScript changes from a reproduced ML miss (0.642627, no calibrated level) to live scan hostile (0.960, L25). The three underlying JavaScript model routes remain below their own hostile cutoffs; aggregate admission is not evidence of behavior.
placement_claim_corrections: A socket receive-to-shell dispatch is remote-command dispatch; a backdoor deployment is not required by its matcher.
Credential collection spanning stored credentials and provider tokens is not confined to a cloud-secret service.
Bitwarden and node-tar test-variable mentions do not identify the scanned program as those products.
Generic quoted host fields, computed awaited calls, !0x0 call arguments, and username XML attributes establish source syntax rather than attacker behavior or a form.
Two withFileTypes strings establish option-name references, not directory reads.
A long Base64-alphabet literal is a static representation observation, not proof of an encoding operation.

Bare Bitwarden name mentions belong with service-name references, beside the existing OnePassword reference; they prove neither application targeting nor product identity. The 102-entry application-target leaf audit found no identical effective matchers to erase.

ancestor_audit.notes: Exact consumers retain relocated observations. The Bitwarden-specific directory exclusion explicitly preserves its former two name observations.
